newsitem.title: JAPAN: FORECAST - Japan Oct-Dec GDP to post steady growth.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Japan Oct-Dec GDP to post steady growth.

text.p: Japan's economy is expected to have posted steady growth in the October-December quarter, but economists are uncertain about whether the economic recovery is as strong as it seems.

"The figures themselves will confirm that the economy is steadily expanding, but we won't know about real economic conditions and whether the recovery is steadfast until we look at data for the April-June and July-September periods," said Tatsushi Shikano, an economist at Yamaichi Research Institute of Securities and Economics Inc.

The Economic Planning Agency is expected to announce gross domestic product (GDP) data for the October-December period either this week or next. It will flag the timing of the announcement 48 hours in advance.

Economists polled by Reuters said on average they expect real GDP for the period to grow 0.8 percent quarter-on-quarter, against 0.1 percent growth in the previous quarter. Forecasts ranged from 0.3 percent to 1.2 percent growth.
Private consumption and external demand are thought to have been the twin engines propelling growth in the fourth quarter of calendar 1996.
A fall in public works spending had the biggest effect in hampering growth, economists said.
Low interest rates and a planned consumption tax increase to five percent from three percent in April accelerated growth in housing investment, they said.

Private consumption is expected to have rebounded from low growth in the previous quarter, when it was dampened by a food poisoning epidemic. The planned tax rise also helped to encourage automobile sales during the quarter, economists said.

Companies have yet to discard their cautious outlook on the economy, but corporate capital spending is expected to have shown steady growth. The planned tax rise is expected to have encouraged continued purchases of machinery before April.

External demand received a boost from the weakness of the yen, which made Japanese products more competitive in overseas markets and put a lid on imports into Japan. Strong demand overseas, especially in the United States, also helped raise car exports, they said.
Public works spending, which had fuelled the earlier stages of the economic recovery, is expected to have fallen considerably in the October-December period.

Economists expect GDP growth in calendar 1996 to be more than three percent and see growth for the fiscal year ending on March 31 at more or less the government forecast of 2.5 percent. Japan's official forecast of real GDP growth for 1997/98 is set at 1.9 percent. Some analysts see this as a realistic number while others doubt if it can be achieved.
